title: Jayden Nelson added to Canada World Cup roster as Marcelo Flores replacement
content:
TORONTO – Jayden Nelson has been added to Canada’s World Cup squad to replace the injured Marcelo Flores.

After missing the cut for Jesse Marsch’s final roster, Nelson has stayed with Canada’s team and played in both of their pre-World Cup friendlies. The Austin FC winger scored the second goal in their 2-0 win over Uzbekistan and came on as a second half substitute in the 1-1 draw against Ireland.

Flores ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament on May 30 while playing in the Concacaf Champions Cup final for Mexico’s Tigres, his final club game of the season. A Canada statement on Tuesday confirmed he had undergone surgery to repair the ligament on June 5.

While Marsch waited to name the creative attacking midfielder’s replacement, in Nelson, the head coach is getting a player who can fulfill his tactical and emotional requirements should the 23-year-old be needed as a substitute in the World Cup.

Nelson has primarily been deployed as a left winger. However he has also played as an attacking central midfielder and a right winger through his seven professional seasons. Versatility in any bench player is a priority for Marsch.

Nelson is one of the quicker players on the Canadian squad and is blessed with an attack-minded mentality. His goal against Uzbekistan was a reminder of his technical qualities. While Nelson might not offer the dribbling skills and wiriness that Flores does, he will be able to meet Marsch’s pressing and intensity demands.

Nelson has been part of Canada’s squad for most of the last nine months, appearing in seven of Canada’s last 11 matches and only missing out on their March international window because of a muscle injury.

The winger has made his case for inclusion in the World Cup squad through his first season with Austin FC as well: he has made the most of the start of his season, averaging 0.4 goals per 90 minutes, second among all Austin players.
